documents.title: Practical Local AI Tools — Tested, Not Just Hyped
documents.summary:
Practical Local AI Tools — Tested, Not Just Hyped

I’m going to share local AI tools and workflows that I have actually installed, tested, or verified through reliable public sources.

The focus is simple: Does it work? What hardware does it need? How fast is it? What are the common traps?

Local AI / Codex

Start with Codex CLI + Ollama + a local model + Web Search.

OpenAI Codex CLI:
https://github.com/openai/codex

Ollama + Codex:
https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/codex

MiniMax H3 / ComfyUI

I will share several H3 workflows and plugins that I have recently installed and successfully tested.

Two-stage latent refinement / acceleration workflow

H3 face repair LoRA

H3 action / combat LoRA workflows

The first recommendation will be the acceleration workflow that gave me a major speed improvement while keeping output quality close to the original workflow.

I will include real generation times, VRAM requirements, image quality differences, and known failure cases.

Local AI Music

For full songs: ACE-Step 1.5

https://github.com/ace-step/ACE-Step-1.5

For instrumental music / sound generation / Audio-to-Audio: Stable Audio 3

https://github.com/Stability-AI/stable-audio-3

One important lesson from testing:

ACE-Step is better suited for song generation.

Stable Audio 3 is useful for instrumental/audio generation, continuation and A2A, but it is not the right tool if your goal is to naturally perform an existing musical score.

documents.title: LingBot-Map — Real-Time 3D Reconstruction
documents.summary:
LingBot-Map — Real-Time 3D Reconstruction

What it does
LingBot-Map reconstructs a 3D scene from images or video in a streaming workflow. It can produce point-cloud style 3D environments and supports long sequences, so it is useful for turning a real location into a rough 3D scene instead of rebuilding everything manually in Blender. The official demo supports both image folders and video input.

Official links
GitHub: LingBot-Map GitHub
Model: LingBot-Map on Hugging Face

Install size
The main model checkpoint is about 4.63 GB. The complete environment will be larger because PyTorch, CUDA-related packages, FlashInfer, visualization libraries and optional rendering dependencies are separate, so I would reserve roughly 10–20 GB for a practical Windows/Linux installation rather than planning around the checkpoint size alone.

## Minimum hardware requirements
## Minimum hardware requirements

LingBot-Map does not currently publish a strict official minimum hardware specification, so it is better to separate the requirements into practical minimum and recommended configurations.

**Minimum practical configuration:**

* **Operating system:** Windows 10/11 with WSL2, or Ubuntu/Linux
* **CPU:** Modern 6-core x86-64 processor, roughly Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 class or better
* **RAM:** **16 GB minimum**, 32 GB recommended
* **GPU:** NVIDIA RTX-series GPU
* **VRAM:** **8 GB can be treated as the minimum practical level**
* **Recommended GPU:** RTX 3060 12 GB, RTX 4060 8 GB, or better
* **More comfortable VRAM:** 16–24 GB
* **Python:** Python 3.10
* **PyTorch:** Current official setup uses PyTorch 2.8.0
* **CUDA:** Current installation examples use CUDA 12.8
* **Storage:** Reserve at least **15–20 GB** for a practical installation
* **Internet connection:** Required for the initial dependency installation and model download

An **8 GB GPU should be considered the practical entry point rather than a guaranteed requirement for every workload**. Low-VRAM setups rely on techniques such as CPU offloading, reduced frame scaling, smaller caches, and more conservative inference settings.

For basic installation and testing:

**RTX 4060 8 GB + 16 GB RAM: usable for experimentation.**

For normal video reconstruction with fewer out-of-memory problems:

**RTX 3060 12 GB / RTX 4070 12 GB + 32 GB RAM: a more realistic recommendation.**

For long sequences, larger scenes, heavier point-cloud rendering, or more comfortable local use:

**16–24 GB VRAM + 32–64 GB RAM: recommended.**

It is important to note that memory usage can increase significantly with longer sequences, higher resolutions, larger caches, and more demanding rendering settings. Therefore, an 8 GB GPU should be viewed as a low-VRAM configuration that may require reduced settings rather than as a full-performance setup.

My assessment
This is more interesting as a 3D scene reconstruction / previs tool than as a robotics tool for your use case. I would not call it a full Blender replacement. It is better at quickly converting a real scene or walkthrough video into usable 3D spatial reference; Blender is still better for precise character placement, props, animation blocking and camera control.

How I recommend using it

Shoot or record a real location
→ LingBot-Map reconstructs the scene
→ inspect the 3D point cloud / camera path
→ use it as the environment reference
→ move into Blender only when you need precise actors, props or camera blocking
→ render previs
→ send the previs/reference into H3

For you, the best use is not “make the final 3D movie with LingBot-Map.”
It is:

real environment → fast 3D reconstruction → previs/reference → H3

That can save a lot of time compared with rebuilding every real location from zero in Blender.
